question: Is the guest-browser FLOW census-miss caused by the selfhost kotoba kernel object route, or by stage history in the profile?

object.route: selfhost (amu selfhost compiler lineage; G1=G2=G3 asserted in prior JUN-31 evidence)

A-selfhost-full-profile.profile: guest-browser full (AIUEOS_GUEST_BROWSER=1, synthetic=0), real virtio-keyboard + virtio-tablet via QMP
A-selfhost-full-profile.stage-order: SCALE(100->125->150->100, SCALE_OK events=16) -> RING -> EDIT -> CLOCK -> SETTINGS(n=4 sets pct=125, written=2, stored=1, frame text-px 668->1757 = 2.63x) -> FLOW

B-selfhost-synthetic-profile.profile: synthetic-input (no scale stage, scale stays pct=100)

C-op-stream-identity.meaning: the drawn op stream is the same in both runs; only the rendered magnification differs

D-object-containment.method: ELF .text extracted from each object; base offset located in KERNEL.ELF; byte compare; reloc-masked clean-window uniqueness search (51 B selfhost window, 28 B committed window)

E-control-cell.status: in-flight at commit time; boot started 2026-10-24 05:13 JST (detached, build/aiueos-d, run log control-run4.log); one earlier attempt (control-run2) stalled at AIUEOS_KOTOBA_ELF_PROCESS_OK = the known #108 HOST-FLAKE-SIGNATURE and was retried, not counted as evidence

attribution: The FLOW census-miss tracks the SETTINGS stage's persisted UI scale (pct=125 active at the FLOW measurement, frame census magnified 2.63-2.66x), not the object route: the op stream is byte-identical, the same object route passes the pin at pct=100, and object containment is byte-proven per image.

gate-proposal.option-a: measure the FLOW census at a fixed pct (restore pct=100 before the FLOW stage) and keep the single pin 3593/a19f95a8
gate-proposal.option-b: scale-indexed pins (pct=100: 3593/a19f95a8; pct=125: 9564/b2fad8a7 as measured here)
gate-proposal.recommendation: option-a: one canonical pin keeps the census comparable across profile changes
gate-proposal.root-cause-timeline: pin calibrated ADR-0234 (90f8b03, 2026-09-25) at pct=100; scale stage landed later in ADR-0261 (62490d0, 2026-10-23 16:32, PR #470) - the FLOW pin predates the stage that changes the scale before FLOW

boundary: kernel/*.c is still compiled by zig cc; the C-free claim covers the compiler lineage and the kotoba object route only. The #108 process-phase stall is a separate known flake and is not used as evidence here.
